fullPassage:
People often omit the period at the end of sentences in single-sentence text messages, which has influenced the way we perceive periods. In an experiment, participants reading text messages found single sentences with a period less sincere than those without one. This could be due to something called "situational code-switching," which simply means that we change how we talk depending on the social setting. For example, the language that students use in the classroom is different from the language they use on the playground. If they talked to their friends the same way they talked to their teachers, it would probably sound strange. Similarly, a person using periods in text messages can cause feelings of awkwardness, just like someone using formal language in a casual setting.

In the 1800s, the people of Ireland used potatoes as their basic food source. Unfortunately, everyone was growing the same type of potato, which meant the crops all had the same genes. The farmers did not realize the danger in this. In the 1840s, a new potato disease struck. The genetically identical potatoes all lacked the ability to fight the disease, so they all rotted. Because people were dependent mainly on potatoes for their food, Ireland suffered a famine in which one in eight people died during the following years. If people had grown many types of potatoes, they could have identified resistant ones and grown more of them, making the famine less serious. Despite knowing this, many countries today take the same risk with their crops.

In 1985, my husband and I moved to his hometown, located in China's Ordas Desert. When I first saw our new home, I burst into tears. There was nothing but sand for miles around. "I wish I could see some plants," I thought. Then one day I saw a small tree growing beside a nearby well. I realized that if this tree could survive, others might be able to, too. I started to plant more trees. At first, many of them ended up buried in sandstorms, but my husband and I eventually managed to get most of the trees to survive. We have now planted more than 600,000 trees in the desert. We have turned one of the most desolate places in China into something beautiful.

Socotra Island, a small island owned by Yemen and located in the Arabian Sea, looks as if it were part of another planet. In fact, it separated from the mainland of Africa six or seven million years ago, causing unique forms of life to develop on it. It is home to about 800 species of rare plants and animals, many of which are found nowhere else on earth. Because the island experiences extreme heat and frequent droughts, many of its plants have evolved unusual appearances. One striking example is the dragon's blood tree. Its branches make it look like a giant umbrella. It gets its name from a thick, red substance that comes out when its bark is cut. When this happens, it appears as if the tree were bleeding.

Everyone on Earth may soon lose one second of time. For the first time ever, scientists are considering subtracting a single second. This is called a "negative leap second," and it may be necessary in 2029 because Earth is rotating slightly faster than before. Surprisingly, without global warming, this time change would likely have been necessary sooner. The reason Earth is spinning faster is the unpredictable behavior of its hot liquid core. This behavior has been causing an increase in speed for approximately 50 years, but the melting of polar ice has been counteracting this effect. Melting ice raises sea levels and shifts the planet's mass away from the poles and toward the equator. This slows the Earth's rotation in the same way that figure skaters spin more slowly when extending their arms outward. Without the melting of polar ice, it is likely that we would need to lose a second in 2026 rather than 2029. "We are headed toward a negative leap second," said one expert. "It's a matter of when."

The origins of flags probably began with warriors decorating their spears with colored ribbons as a way of distinguishing one army from another. This practice was adopted by early explorers, who started using flags to show who newly discovered lands belonged to. During the modern era, flags became a symbol of individual nations, and it has become accepted that every country must have its own flag. Most of these national flags are roughly the same size and shape. They commonly feature bold colors and simple patterns, as flags with intricate patterns would appear distorted when blowing in the wind.

Around 2.35 billion years ago, Earth's atmosphere underwent a significant transition: It went from being oxygen-free to possessing a small percentage of oxygen. This change was partly due to tiny organisms known as cyanobacteria. Cyanobacteria, which evolved approximately 2.7 billion years ago, took in water to obtain hydrogen. This allowed them to assimilate carbon from CO₂ in the atmosphere. They then released oxygen as waste. But how could such tiny creatures have caused such a huge change in the planet? It is believed that the amount of oxygen cyanobacteria released slowly increased over hundreds of millions of years. Over this period, it accumulated in Earth's oceans, oxygenating the water. Eventually, the oceans' accumulated oxygen began to escape into the atmosphere. There, it reacted with methane, gradually displacing it. Had there been no cyanobacteria, oxygen might never have become a major component of Earth's atmosphere.

Being alone makes us more creative. Many great artists and thinkers throughout history have lived by themselves. When we are alone, we have fewer distractions. This allows our thoughts to run free without interruption or judgment. Creative people have entire worlds inside their heads, and being alone gives them the opportunity to bring ideas from this inner world into the real world. Steve Wozniak, for example, invented the Apple computer sitting alone at a desk. He says his creativity came from being introverted as a child. Had it not been for his shyness, he might not have become a computer expert. However, this does not mean we should stop working together with others. Had it not been for Wozniak's collaboration with Steve Jobs, he could not have started his own business. Therefore, we should seek out solitude, but only when we need it.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) sincere=진심 어린 / rude=무례한 (B) strange=이상한 / natural=자연스러운 (C) casual=격식 없는 / formal=격식 있는

③ sincere—strange—casual: 덜 '진심 어린', '이상하게' 들림, '격식 없는' 상황 ←정답
④ rude—natural—formal: (A)(B)(C) 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 덜 '진심 어린'(sincere) → '이상하게'(strange) 들림 → '격식 없는'(casual) 상황

questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 type의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.tip: type의 다의어: 같은 종류(명사) vs 타자를 치다(동사)

questions.passage: Socotra Island, a small island owned by Yemen and located in the Arabian Sea, looks as if it were part of another __________. In fact, it separated from the mainland of Africa six or seven million years ago, causing unique forms of life to develop on it. It is home to about 800 species of rare plants and animals, many of which are found nowhere else on earth. Because the island experiences extreme heat and frequent droughts, many of its plants have evolved unusual appearances. One striking example is the dragon's blood tree. Its branches make it look like a giant umbrella. It gets its name from a thick, red substance that comes out when its bark is cut. When this happens, it appears as if the tree were bleeding.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ocean=바다 / country=나라 / forest=숲 / planet=행성
det.analysis:
① ocean: '다른 바다의 일부'? 외계 같다는 묘사와 안 맞음
② country: '다른 나라의 일부'? 외계 느낌을 살리지 못함
③ forest: '다른 숲의 일부'? 부적절
④ planet: 섬이 '다른 행성(planet)'의 일부처럼 보인다 = 외계 같은 독특함 강조 ←정답
det.tip: 외계 같은 풍경 → looks as if it were part of another planet(행성)

questions.passage: Everyone on Earth may soon lose one second of time. For the first time ever, scientists are considering subtracting a single second. This is called a "negative leap second," and it may be (A)[necessary / optional] in 2029 because Earth is rotating slightly (B)[slower / faster] than before. Surprisingly, without global warming, this time change would likely have been necessary sooner. The reason Earth is spinning faster is the unpredictable behavior of its hot liquid core. This behavior has been causing an (C)[increase / decrease] in speed for approximately 50 years, but the melting of polar ice has been counteracting this effect. Melting ice raises sea levels and shifts the planet's mass away from the poles and toward the equator. This slows the Earth's rotation in the same way that figure skaters spin more slowly when extending their arms outward. Without the melting of polar ice, it is likely that we would need to lose a second in 2026 rather than 2029. "We are headed toward a negative leap second," said one expert. "It's a matter of when."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) necessary=필요한 / optional=선택적인 (B) faster=더 빠른 / slower=더 느린 (C) increase=증가 / decrease=감소
det.analysis:
(A) 지구가 빨라졌기 때문에 1초를 빼는 것이 '필요할(necessary)' 수 있다는 흐름이라 necessary
(B) 지구가 이전보다 '더 빠르게(faster)' 자전하고 있다는 글의 핵심이라 faster
(C) 핵의 활동이 속도의 '증가(increase)'를 일으켜 왔다는 내용이라 increase
④ necessary — faster — increase ←정답
det.tip: 조정이 필요(necessary) → 빨라짐(faster) → 속도 증가(increase)

questions.passage: The origins of flags probably began with warriors decorating their spears with colored ribbons as a way of (A)[combining / distinguishing] one army from another. This practice was adopted by early explorers, who started using flags to show who newly discovered lands belonged to. During the modern era, flags became a symbol of (B)[individual / collective] nations, and it has become accepted that every country must have its own flag. Most of these national flags are roughly the same size and shape. They commonly feature bold colors and (C)[simple / complex] patterns, as flags with intricate patterns would appear distorted when blowing in the wind.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) distinguishing=구별하는 / combining=결합하는 (B) individual=각각의 / collective=공동의 (C) simple=단순한 / complex=복잡한
det.analysis:
① combining—individual—simple: (A) 한 군대를 다른 군대와 '결합하는' 것이 아니라 '구별하는(distinguishing)' 방법임
② distinguishing—collective—complex: (B) 각각의(individual) 국가의 상징이며, (C) 복잡한 무늬는 왜곡되므로 단순한(simple) 무늬가 맞음
③ distinguishing—individual—simple: 군대를 구별 + 각각의 국가 상징 + 단순한 무늬 ←정답
④ combining—collective—complex: 세 곳 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 군대를 distinguishing(구별) + individual(각각의) 국가 + simple(단순한) 무늬

questions.passage: Around 2.35 billion years ago, Earth's atmosphere underwent a (A)[significant / minor] transition: It went from being oxygen-free to possessing a small percentage of oxygen. This change was partly due to tiny organisms known as cyanobacteria. Cyanobacteria, which evolved approximately 2.7 billion years ago, took in water to (B)[lose / obtain] hydrogen. This allowed them to assimilate carbon from CO₂ in the atmosphere. They then (C)[absorbed / released] oxygen as waste. But how could such tiny creatures have caused such a huge change in the planet? It is believed that the amount of oxygen cyanobacteria released slowly increased over hundreds of millions of years. Over this period, it accumulated in Earth's oceans, oxygenating the water. Eventually, the oceans' accumulated oxygen began to escape into the atmosphere. There, it reacted with methane, gradually displacing it. Had there been no cyanobacteria, oxygen might never have become a major component of Earth's atmosphere.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) significant=상당한 / minor=사소한 (B) obtain=얻다 / lose=잃다 (C) released=방출했다 / absorbed=흡수했다
det.analysis:
① minor—obtain—released: (A) 대기의 '상당한(significant)' 변화라 significant가 맞음
② significant—obtain—released: 상당한 변화 + 수소를 '얻기(obtain)' 위해 + 산소를 '방출(released)' ←정답
③ significant—lose—absorbed: (B)(C) 수소를 '얻는(obtain)' 것이고, 산소를 '방출(released)'함
④ minor—lose—absorbed: 세 자리 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: significant(상당한) 변화, obtain(얻다) 수소, released(방출) 산소

questions.passage: Being alone makes us more creative. Many great artists and thinkers throughout history have lived by themselves. When we are alone, we have fewer distractions. This allows our thoughts to run free without interruption or judgment. Creative people have entire worlds inside their heads, and being alone gives them the opportunity to bring ideas from this inner world into the real world. Steve Wozniak, for example, invented the Apple computer sitting alone at a desk. He says his creativity came from being introverted as a child. Had it not been for his shyness, he might not have become a computer expert. However, this does not mean we should stop working together with others. Had it not been for Wozniak's collaboration with Steve Jobs, he could not have started his own business. Therefore, we should <u>seek out</u> solitude, but only when we need it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 seek out와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: seek out=찾아내다 / look for=찾다 / give up=포기하다 / run from=~에서 도망치다 / laugh at=~을 비웃다
det.analysis:
① look for: 찾다 — seek out(찾아내다)의 동의어 ←정답
② give up: 포기하다 — 찾는 것과 반대
③ run from: ~에서 도망치다 — 찾는 것과 반대
④ laugh at: 비웃다 — 의미 다름
det.tip: seek out(찾아내다) = look for(찾다). give up·run from은 반대

questions.passage: People often ①<u>omit</u> the period at the end of sentences in single-sentence text messages, which has influenced the way we perceive periods. In an experiment, participants reading text messages found single sentences with a period less sincere than those without one. This could be due to something called "situational code-switching," which simply means that we change how we talk depending on the social setting. For example, the language that students use in the classroom is different from the language they use on the playground. If they talked to their friends the same way they talked to their teachers, it would probably sound ②<u>normal</u>. Similarly, a person using periods in text messages can cause feelings of ③<u>awkwardness</u>, just like someone using ④<u>formal</u> language in a casual setting.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① omit=생략하다 ② normal=평범한 → strange(이상한) (부적절) ③ awkwardness=어색함 ④ formal=격식 있는
det.analysis:
① omit: 마침표를 '생략'함 — 적절
② normal: 친구에게 선생님에게 하듯 말하면 '이상하게(strange)' 들린다는 흐름이므로 평범하게(normal)는 반대 ←정답
③ awkwardness: 격식 있는 말을 격식 없는 상황에 쓰면 '어색함'을 줌 — 적절
④ formal: '격식 있는' 언어 — 적절
det.tip: 친구에게 선생님처럼 말하면 '이상하게'(strange) 들림. normal(평범한)은 정반대

questions.passage: In the 1800s, the people of Ireland used potatoes as their basic food source. Unfortunately, everyone was growing the same type of potato, which meant the crops all had the same ①<u>genes</u>. The farmers did not realize the danger in this. In the 1840s, a new potato disease ②<u>struck</u>. The genetically identical potatoes all ③<u>gained</u> the ability to fight the disease, so they all rotted. Because people were dependent mainly on potatoes for their food, Ireland ④<u>suffered</u> a famine in which one in eight people died during the following years. If people had grown many types of potatoes, they could have identified resistant ones and grown more of them, making the famine less serious. Despite knowing this, many countries today take the same risk with their crops.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① genes=유전자 ② struck=덮쳤다 ③ lacked→gained (부적절) ④ suffered=겪었다
det.analysis:
① genes: 작물이 모두 같은 유전자를 가졌다 — 적절
② struck: 새로운 병이 덮쳤다 — 적절
③ gained: 감자가 병과 싸울 능력을 '얻었다'? 그렇다면 썩지 않았을 텐데 뒤에 '모두 썩었다'가 이어지므로 능력이 '없었다(lacked)'가 원문 ←정답
④ suffered: 아일랜드가 기근을 겪었다 — 적절
det.tip: 능력을 gained(얻음)했다면 썩지 않음. 뒤에 '썩었다'가 오므로 lacked(없었다)가 맞음

questions.passage: In 1985, my husband and I moved to his hometown, located in China's Ordas Desert. When I first saw our new home, I burst into tears. There was nothing but sand for miles around. "I wish I could see some plants," I thought. Then one day I saw a small tree growing beside a nearby well. I ①<u>realized</u> that if this tree could survive, others might be able to, too. I ②<u>started</u> to plant more trees. At first, many of them ended up ③<u>buried</u> in sandstorms, but my husband and I ④<u>immediately</u> managed to get most of the trees to survive. We have now planted more than 600,000 trees in the desert. We have turned one of the most desolate places in China into something beautiful.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① realized=깨달았다 ② started=시작했다 ③ buried=파묻힌 ④ eventually→immediately (부적절)
det.analysis:
① realized: 나무가 살면 다른 것도 가능함을 깨달음 — 적절
② started: 더 많은 나무를 심기 시작함 — 적절
③ buried: 처음엔 많은 나무가 모래폭풍에 파묻힘 — 적절
④ immediately: '처음엔(At first) 파묻혔지만 즉시(immediately) 대부분 살려냈다'? 오랜 노력 끝에 결국(eventually)이 원문 ←정답
det.tip: At first(처음엔) 실패했지만 eventually(결국/마침내) 성공. immediately(즉시)는 '처음엔 실패'와 모순

questions.passage: Socotra Island, a small island owned by Yemen and located in the Arabian Sea, looks as if it were part of another planet. In fact, it separated from the mainland of Africa six or seven million years ago, causing unique forms of life to develop on it. It is home to about 800 species of rare plants and animals, many of which are found nowhere else on earth. Because the island experiences extreme heat and frequent droughts, many of its plants have evolved unusual appearances. One <u>striking</u> example is the dragon's blood tree. Its branches make it look like a giant umbrella. It gets its name from a thick, red substance that comes out when its bark is cut. When this happens, it appears as if the tree were bleeding.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 striking과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: striking=인상적인 / remarkable=주목할 만한 / dull=밋밋한 / tiny=아주 작은 / quiet=조용한
det.analysis:
① remarkable: 주목할 만한 — striking의 동의어 ←정답
② dull: 밋밋한 — striking과 반대
③ tiny: 아주 작은 — 의미 다름
④ quiet: 조용한 — 의미 다름
det.tip: 인상적인(striking) = remarkable(주목할 만한). dull은 반대라 오답
